Formulas are explained in our own words. Data comes from Yahoo Finance; the book’s authors are not assessing these companies.
sg&a = selling, general and administrati: SG&A = selling, general and administrative expenses; D&A = depreciation and amortisation, sourced from the cash flow statement. Debt means interest-bearing debt; the book’s definition uses all liabilities. Treasury stock is added back only when its carrying amount is reported; retired shares cannot be reconstructed from annual buybacks. Non-positive denominators produce no ratio.
the book also considers ten-year earning: The book also considers ten-year earnings, EPS, retained-earnings and capex trends. This short quarterly history cannot establish them; capex/net income here covers only the selected period. The 39-criterion score remains a separate multi-year snapshot, not a score for this quarter. The equity-bond approach, yield on cost and buy/sell decisions also require a purchase price, bond yield and future assumptions. Use the valuation lab for scenario analysis.
